§7.2.2 Displayed Equations

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

text-displayed-equations · text formatting math

✅ Normative

Displayed mathematics MUST be written as LaTeX inside $$ … $$. Its printed equation number MUST follow the closing delimiter as plain text in the same formula block: $$ … $$ (1).

A displayed equation is set on its own line, usually centred, often with a number at the right margin — (1), (2) — that the prose cites.

                 ΔE = ΔE⁰ − (RT / m·F) [ ln(θ / 1−θ) + fθ + gθ^(3/2) ]          (1)

Requirements

  • The delimiters are those of Inline Equations§7.2.6: $$ … $$, never single $.
  • The equation number MUST be kept. It is content — "as shown in (1)" appears in the prose — and dropping it is the one option that loses something (never drop).
  • The number MUST be written after the closing $$, as plain text, in the same block — not inside the LaTeX, and not as a separate paragraph. The Formula block includes its number; see Block Classes§5.3.
  • An unnumbered display MUST NOT be given a number.

✅ Sample — numbered equations in a two-column article

Two display equations, numbered (1) and (2) at the right margin, each cited in the surrounding text. Equation (2) spans the full column width and wraps after ⇒; the wrap is typesetting, so the LaTeX is one line. The symbol cited in the prose after (1) is itself maths and takes the inline form.

Expected Markdown · excerpt, right column

UPD represents a potential dependent adsorption with great sensitivity and selectivity towards the nature of the metal surface and its termination. The complexity of the voltammetry features arises from the existence of one or more UPD ML superstructures22,23 and/or one or more UPD MLs formed.24,25

$$\Delta E = \Delta E^{0}_{\theta \to 0} - (RT / mF) \cdot [\ln(\theta/(1-\theta)) + f\theta + g\theta^{3/2}]$$ (1)

Here the $$\Delta E^{0}_{\theta \to 0}$$ term represents the underpotential of the most positive stripping peak of the UPD adlayer where its coverage approaches zero. The term f is the Temkin parameter describing the attractive UPD ML–substrate interactions, as given in Eq. (1).

…

The UPD ML coverage can be controlled effectively down to a fraction of a monolayer by proper choice of an underpotential. The amount of deposited P is controlled by the reaction stoichiometry and the coverage of the UPD ML of metal M. The most general formulation of the SLRR reaction is given by the following equation:16

$$(\theta_{M} \cdot \rho_{M}^{\mathrm{UPD}}) \cdot M^{0}{\mathrm{UPD}}/S(h,k,l) + (\theta{M} \cdot \rho_{M}^{\mathrm{UPD}}) \cdot (m/p)P^{p+}{\mathrm{solv}} \Rightarrow (\theta{M} \cdot \rho_{M}^{\mathrm{UPD}}) \cdot M^{m+}{\mathrm{solv}} + (\theta{M} \cdot \rho_{M}^{\mathrm{UPD}}) \cdot (m/p)P^{0}_{s}/S(h,k,l)$$ (2)

Here the $$\Delta E^{0}_{\theta \to 0}$$ term represents the underpotential of the most positive stripping peak of the UPD adlayer where its coverage approaches zero. The term f is the Temkin parameter describing the attractive UPD ML–substrate interactions, as given in Eq. (1).

The amount of deposited P is controlled by the reaction stoichiometry and the coverage of the UPD ML of metal M. The most general formulation of the SLRR reaction is given by the following equation:<sup>16</sup>

✅ Sample — a typewritten paper

Equation V = pu_y numbered (2) at the right margin, then an unnumbered display ½ mV², in a scanned typewritten proceedings page. Run-in underlined headings, also set in italic, open two paragraphs.

Expected Markdown · excerpt

…

Velocity Spectra. Another method of presenting the same data is of interest here. This method involves the concept of a spectral velocity for the elasto-plastic system. The definition which is most convenient is to define the spectral velocity V by the relationship

$$V = pu_{y}$$ (2)

where p denotes the undamped circular natural frequency of the system. Then the quantity

$$\frac{1}{2} mV^{2}$$

represents the maximum recoverable strain energy of the system. It should be noted that this definition of the spectral velocity for the elasto-plastic system is consistent with that used for elastic systems, since in an elastic system the yield deformation may be taken equal to the maximum elastic deformation.

Relation Between Input Motion and Response Values. It is convenient to plot velocity spectra on a four-way logarithmic grid, so that displacement, velocity, acceleration and period may all be read from a single chart.

Markdown source
<!-- … -->


<u>Velocity Spectra.</u> Another method of presenting the same data is of interest here. This method involves the concept of a spectral velocity for the elasto-plastic system. The definition which is most convenient is to define the spectral velocity V by the relationship


$$V = pu_{y}$$ (2)


where p denotes the undamped circular natural frequency of the system. Then the quantity


$$\frac{1}{2} mV^{2}$$


represents the maximum recoverable strain energy of the system. It should be noted that this definition of the spectral velocity for the elasto-plastic system is consistent with that used for elastic systems, since in an elastic system the yield deformation may be taken equal to the maximum elastic deformation.


<u>Relation Between Input Motion and Response Values.</u> It is convenient to plot velocity spectra on a four-way logarithmic grid, so that displacement, velocity, acceleration and period may all be read from a single chart.

Formulas drawn as boxes

A formula laid out as boxes joined by operators is still an equation.

  • A boxed arithmetic formula MUST be written in $$ … $$, keeping every printed operand, operator and label; the box labels become the operands.
  • Where the boxes express a process rather than an equation, the region is a diagram and MUST be rendered as a diagram block instead — see Images and Figures§12.1.2.

✅ Sample — a formula drawn as boxes


Source: Defense Business Practice Implementation Board, Financial Indicators Task Group, Report FY03-1, "Capital Asset Growth Rate" (public domain)

A growth-rate calculation laid out as black boxes: two boxes joined by - over a rule, a third box beneath, each box holding a labelled sum in bold white type. It is a fraction with no LaTeX on the page. The grouping the boxes print becomes parentheses in the numerator.
